# AGENTS.md - JSHack Field Manual

JSHack is a zero-dependency browser roguelike: pure JavaScript, pure ES modules,
ECS architecture, Deno tooling. This file is optimized for coding agents. Prefer
the commands below over manual spelunking.

Deeper docs:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [SEPARATION_MANIFEST.md](docs/architecture/SEPARATION_MANIFEST.md)
- [RUNTIME_TOPOLOGY_DOCTRINE.md](docs/architecture/RUNTIME_TOPOLOGY_DOCTRINE.md)
- [TEN_COMMANDMENTS.md](docs/architecture/TEN_COMMANDMENTS.md)
- [ecs-js/AGENTS.md](src/lib/ecs-js/AGENTS.md)

---

## Hard Laws

- **No build step.** Pure ES modules. No webpack, babel, JSX, TypeScript, or
  bundling.
- **Deno, not Node.** Tests and tools run with Deno. Default test command:
  `deno test --allow-read`.
- **JavaScript only.** Keep source as `.js` / `.mjs`.
- **Mobile-first.** Touch is primary; desktop keyboard is secondary.
- **Separation is law.** `rules/` never imports `display/` or `bridge/`;
  `display/` never imports `rules/`; `bridge/` projects read-only rule state.
- **No system-to-system calls.** Systems communicate with `world.emit` /
  `world.on`; scheduler owns ordering.
- **New events use concrete event classes.** Any new event contract must define
  a concrete `EcsEvent` class and emit an instance with
  `world.emit(new Event(...))`. Do not introduce string-only events or parallel
  string re-emits for new contracts.
- **Touched listener installers use canonical extensions.** Any new listener
  installer, or any existing listener installer touched during a task, must use
  `defineExtension(...)` and `world.install(...)` for idempotent installation.
  Do not add new bespoke symbol-guard installers.
- **No swallowed event failures.** Do not add `emitSafe`-style wrappers around
  `world.emit`.
- **No new world-attached state.** Do not attach simulation state to `world`
  with symbol or property keys (`world[...]`, `ctx.world[...]`). Use ECS
  components for state; when the state is genuinely world-scoped, model it as an
  explicit singleton entity/component and document the allowance. Existing
  world-attached state is a ratcheted architecture debt tracked by
  `ratchets/worldStateAttachmentRatchet.test.mjs`.
- **Determinism is sacred.** In rules simulation use `world.rand()`, never
  `Math.random()`. No timers/fetch/promises/async in systems.
- **Integer grid only.** World coords may be negative. Do not clamp to `>= 0`;
  normalize with `Number.isFinite(v) ? (v | 0) : fallback`.
- **One canonical path.** Spawn, damage, spell cast, status application,
  inventory transfer, and materialization paths must delegate to the canonical
  implementation.
- **Runtime multiplicity is child entities.** Runtime
  effects/procs/sockets/enchantments are child topology, not arrays on parent
  components.
- **ECS-js is vendored.** Do not edit `src/lib/ecs-js/` unless fixing the ECS
  library itself.
- **Authoring discipline.** Do not touch unrelated code. Do not make changes
  that do nothing. Always match the formatting preferences that already exist;
  be a chameleon.
- **Commit messages.** Every commit message must be lowercase and use a
  conventional type prefix such as `feat:`, `docs:`, `fix:`, `arch:`,
  `refactor:`, `test:`, `perf:`, `ci:`, or `chore:`.
- **Do not format code unless explicitly requested.** Do not run `deno fmt` or
  any other formatter as part of implementation or verification. Preserve the
  existing formatting and keep diffs limited to the requested functional edits.
- **Search before writing.** Extend existing patterns. Do exactly what was
  asked; no opportunistic content wiring or unrelated cleanup.
- **New authored content targets new runs.** Do not add migrations or repair
  paths for existing saved runs when adding quests, landmarks, dungeon
  entrances, or other authored world content. New content is expected to
  appear in newly generated runs; validate the fresh-run path instead.
- **Capture skills incrementally.** When a task reveals a reusable tool,
  process, authoring path, verification command, or failure mode, record the
  proven practice in the smallest relevant `.agents/skills/` guide as part of
  the task or its immediate follow-up. Do not make broad skills coverage a
  prerequisite for feature work, and do not document speculative patterns.
- **Verify in proportion to the change.** Run focused tests and guardrails that
  cover the touched behavior. Do not run the full runtime suite by default; it
  is allowed only when explicitly requested or when the change genuinely needs
  broad regression coverage. Always report what was run and any known or
  observed failures.
- **Content authoring comes first.** When adding content-facing behavior,
  prefer small authored definitions, generic affordances, and reusable engine
  surfaces over bespoke wiring. If a feature needs UI or interaction glue, ask
  whether `defineInteractable()`, content DSLs, or an existing canonical
  pipeline should own it before adding one-off main/display code.

### Agent tool ownership

Every current `tools/` entry is classified in
[docs/architecture/AGENT_TOOL_OWNERSHIP.md](docs/architecture/AGENT_TOOL_OWNERSHIP.md).
Agent-facing deterministic inspection, runtime-proof, and monster-training
implementations are colocated with their owning skill under
`.agents/skills/<owner>/scripts/`. General repository/CI/developer tooling,
browser authoring tools, audio asset tooling, and other independent-lifecycle
utilities remain in `tools/` with their rationale recorded in that matrix.
There is one canonical implementation per moved tool; stable `deno task`
interfaces remain the compatibility boundary.

For the complete routing workflow, use
[`.agents/skills/agent-tools/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/agent-tools/SKILL.md).

### Runtime Proving and Performance

Use [`.agents/skills/runtime-tools/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/runtime-tools/SKILL.md)
when static inspection must be followed by a seeded headless run, agent-bridge
trace, scheduler profile, or performance baseline.

### Focused Tests

```bash
deno test --allow-read tests/separationBoundaries.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/determinismArchitectureGuards.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/schedulerArchitectureGuards.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/dealDamage.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/castSpell.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/interaction.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/movementRefactored.test.mjs
deno test --allow-read tests/contentCatalogCanonical.test.mjs
```

Prefer the smallest meaningful verification set: changed test files, adjacent
behavior tests, architecture guardrails, and targeted audit tools. If you do run
broad runtime coverage, use `deno test --allow-read --no-check` and treat
pre-existing failures as baseline debt to report, not as permission to obscure
new failures.

Plain `deno test --allow-read` may fail during type-check on non-game packaging
scripts before tests run. Use `--no-check` for runtime coverage when type-check
is not the thing being tested.

### Fast Greps

```bash
rg -n "world\\.(on|emit)\\s*\\(" src --glob '!src/lib/**'
rg -n "registerSystem\\(|install[A-Za-z0-9_]+\\(" src/main/scheduler.js
rg -n "Math\\.random|Date\\.now|setTimeout|setInterval|Promise|fetch|await" src/rules
rg -n "from ['\"].*display|from ['\"].*bridge" src/rules
rg -n "from ['\"].*rules" src/display
```

---

## Architecture Map

```text
rules/    deterministic simulation; no DOM, display, timers, async systems
bridge/   read-only projection from rules state to WorldView DTOs
display/  presentation only; reads WorldView and main-provided contracts
main/     wiring, lifecycle, input dispatch, scheduler setup
shared/   pure math/grid utilities; no ECS or DOM
lib/      vendored ecs-js and deity-js
content/  DSL-authored content definitions and content helpers
```

Five scheduler phases are declared in
[src/main/scheduler.js](src/main/scheduler.js):

```text
ai       intent producers
intents  movement/combat/use/cast/interaction consumers
effects  per-turn derived effects and world simulation
scripts  content DSL tick hooks
cleanup  entity removal, lifespan, spatial sync
```

The bridge contract is
[src/bridge/schema/worldView.js](src/bridge/schema/worldView.js). Display must
not push tags onto entity records; tag projection belongs in the bridge.

---

## Common Locations

| Need                 | Start Here                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Scheduler order      | [src/main/scheduler.js](src/main/scheduler.js)                                                                                                         |
| WorldView projection | [src/bridge/schema/worldView.js](src/bridge/schema/worldView.js)                                                                                       |
| Systems              | [src/rules/systems/](src/rules/systems/)                                                                                                               |
| Components           | [src/rules/components/](src/rules/components/)                                                                                                         |
| Monsters             | [src/content/monsters/](src/content/monsters/), [src/rules/data/monsters.js](src/rules/data/monsters.js)                                               |
| Items                | [src/content/items/](src/content/items/), [src/rules/data/itemCatalog.js](src/rules/data/itemCatalog.js)                                               |
| Spells               | [src/rules/data/spells.js](src/rules/data/spells.js), [src/rules/scripts/spells.js](src/rules/scripts/spells.js)                                       |
| Interaction payloads | [src/rules/content/interaction/interactPayloads.js](src/rules/content/interaction/interactPayloads.js)                                                 |
| Damage               | [src/rules/utils/dealDamage.js](src/rules/utils/dealDamage.js)                                                                                         |
| Status semantics     | [src/rules/utils/effectSemantics.js](src/rules/utils/effectSemantics.js), [src/rules/utils/statusFacade.js](src/rules/utils/statusFacade.js)           |
| Spatial queries      | [src/rules/utils/spatialIndex.js](src/rules/utils/spatialIndex.js)                                                                                     |
| Inventory            | [src/rules/utils/inventoryFacade.js](src/rules/utils/inventoryFacade.js), [src/rules/utils/inventoryVirtuals.js](src/rules/utils/inventoryVirtuals.js) |
| Materials/gems       | [src/rules/data/materials.js](src/rules/data/materials.js), [src/rules/data/gems.js](src/rules/data/gems.js)                                           |
| Dungeon tiles/FOV    | [src/rules/environment/dungeon/](src/rules/environment/dungeon/)                                                                                       |
| Quests/dialog        | [src/rules/quests/](src/rules/quests/), [src/rules/dialogues/](src/rules/dialogues/)                                                                   |
| Display event wiring | [src/display/ui/wiring/](src/display/ui/wiring/)                                                                                                       |
| Audio wiring         | [src/display/audio/](src/display/audio/)                                                                                                               |

---

## Patterns That Matter

### Content-First Engine Work

The architecture exists to make strange rules cheap to author. Before adding a
new one-off interaction, modal, command, or UI bridge, look for the content
surface that should own it:

- `defineInteractable()` for object affordances, verbs, prompts, and hooks.
- Content DSL/catalog files for canonical item, monster, spell, and feature
  authoring.
- Existing rules pipelines for spawn, damage, use/apply, status, inventory, and
  transitions.

For item mechanic copy, authored prose must use placeholders for mechanical
values (for example `{duration}` or `{effect.damage.amount}`). Resolve those
values from the canonical ability/effect/stat metadata; never duplicate live
numbers inside English descriptions or display formats.

The standard is not "least code today." The standard is whether the next weird
rule becomes small, explicit, composable, deterministic, and inspectable.

### Incremental Skill Capture

Treat each completed issue as an opportunity to improve the next agent's
starting position. During implementation, note the canonical files and paths,
required tools or commands, architectural invariants, useful fixtures, and
failure modes that were discovered. After the behavior is proven, update the
smallest relevant skill—or create one only when a repeated workflow justifies
it—with those verified details and a focused validation recipe.

Skill capture is evidence-based documentation, not a parallel architecture
project. Keep feature delivery moving when a skill does not yet exist, and
avoid turning one issue into a repository-wide skills rewrite.

### Listener Installers

Use `defineExtension(...)` and `world.install(...)` for listener installers:

```js
import { defineExtension } from "../../lib/ecs-js/index.js";
import { FeatureHappened } from "../../events/FeatureHappened.js";

export const featureListeners = defineExtension(
  "jshack:domain:feature",
  (world) => {
    world.on(FeatureHappened, (event) => {});
  },
);
```

Install listeners with `world.install(featureListeners)` from `configureWorld()`
unless the feature is display/main wiring.

### New Systems

1. Add `src/rules/systems/mySystem.js`.
2. Register it in [src/main/scheduler.js](src/main/scheduler.js) in the right
   phase.
3. Add a focused test in `tests/`.
4. Run `deno test --allow-read tests/mySystem.test.mjs`.

### Spatial Queries

Use `forEachInRadius`, `forEachInRect`, or tile query helpers. Do not full-scan
`world.query()` for proximity-sensitive behavior.

### Spawning

Route through canonical archetypes/materialization helpers. Debug spawns,
dungeon population, and spawner children must have parity tests if they differ.

### Events

New event contracts must be concrete `EcsEvent` classes:

```js
import { EcsEvent } from "../lib/ecs-js/index.js";

export class FeatureHappened extends EcsEvent {
  constructor(payload = {}) {
    super();
    this.actorId = Number(payload.actorId || 0) | 0;
    Object.freeze(this);
  }
}

world.emit(new FeatureHappened({ actorId }));
```

If an event should be visible to display/audio/messages, verify the complete
producer/consumer wiring with:

```bash
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format csv --event event:name
```

---

## Red Tests

Tests can be stale. Do not make tests green by restoring old behavior unless the
user explicitly asks for that behavior.

Classify failures:

- **Real bug:** fix implementation.
- **Stale expectation:** update the test to current intended behavior.
- **Ambiguous:** stop and ask.

Prefer invariant tests over brittle snapshots: determinism, reachability,
bounds, parity, layer boundaries, canonical paths.

---

## Merge Checklist

- [ ] No build step or new dependency pipeline.
- [ ] No `Math.random()` in rules simulation.
- [ ] No `emitSafe` or swallowed event errors.
- [ ] No new `world[...]` / `ctx.world[...]` simulation state; use ECS
      components or an explicit singleton component.
- [ ] No direct system-to-system calls.
- [ ] No illegal layer imports.
- [ ] New or touched listeners use `defineExtension(...)` and
      `world.install(...)`.
- [ ] New systems are registered and tested.
- [ ] Spawn paths use canonical constructors/materializers.
- [ ] Event wiring checked with `.agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs`.
- [ ] Agent health checked with `.agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/agent-health.mjs`.
- [ ] Focused tests and relevant guardrails were run and reported.

## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/home/pjensen/.codex/skills`
- `r1` = `/home/pjensen/.codex/skills/.system`
- `r2` = `/home/pjensen/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote`
- `r3` = `/home/pjensen/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/sites/1.1.6/skills`
- `r4` = `/home/pjensen/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/work-pets/0.1.6/skills`
- `r5` = `/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/.agents/skills`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r1/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r1/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r1/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r1/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
- add-item: Add a new item to the roguelike dungeon crawler (file: r5/add-item/SKILL.md)
- add-monster: Add a new monster to the roguelike dungeon crawler (file: r5/add-monster/SKILL.md)
- add-spell: Add a new spell to the roguelike dungeon crawler (file: r5/add-spell/SKILL.md)

- aura-authoring: Add or extend persistent aura-backed abilities and content in the JSHack roguelike, including affected-entity visuals. (file: r5/aura-authoring/SKILL.md)
- explain: Explains the intent behind source code by finding original session transcripts. Use explain with a function, file, or line of code to understand why it exists. (file: r5/explain/SKILL.md)
- monster-ai-training: Run bounded, seeded mini-simulation training for JSHack tactical and caster monster neural policies. (file: r5/monster-ai-training/SKILL.md)
- quest-authoring: Use when adding a quest-backed dungeon, landmark destination, quest giver, encounter roster, or multi-stage content arc to JSHack. (file: r5/quest-authoring/SKILL.md)
- recall: Use when the user describes a task and wants to know whether something similar has been done before, then turn the closest prior session into a task playbook. Triggers on phrases like "have we done this before", "recall how we did X", "find similar work", "any precedent for", "has anyone solved", "is there a template for", and "how did we do this last time" (file: r5/recall/SKILL.md)
- replay: Use when the user wants to step through a feature's checkpoints chronologically, pausing at each step to ask questions. Triggers on phrases like "replay <feature>", "walk me through how X was built", "show me the journey of", "step me through how Y was implemented", and "replay the last week" (file: r5/replay/SKILL.md)
- review: Review code changes on the current branch using checkpoint transcript context to understand developer intent before auditing the diff. Use when the user asks for a code review, wants to review branch changes, or asks to audit recent work before merging. (file: r5/review/SKILL.md)
- runtime-tools: Use JSHack's deterministic headless runtime, agent bridge, profiling, and benchmark tools to prove gameplay behavior and measure runtime performance. (file: r5/runtime-tools/SKILL.md)
- search: Use when the user wants to find prior work, checkpoints, or agent conversations by topic, repo, branch, author, or recent time window (file: r5/search/SKILL.md)

(file: r0/basin/SKILL.md)

(file: r0/cf-cli/SKILL.md)
- cloudflare: Discover and choose Cloudflare products for apps, APIs, AI agents, storage, networking, and security. - gateway-workers: Build, debug, or review Cloudflare Workers invoked by the Forward action in Gateway HTTP policies, including the GatewayMiddleware entrypoint, Gateway types, context, and continuation. (file: r0/gateway-workers/SKILL.md)
- k2: Build and troubleshoot Cloudflare K2 or K2 Streams durable logs. Use for stream setup, producing from Workers or HTTP, configuring retention and inputs, and consuming through subscriptions. (file: r0/k2/SKILL.md)
- nextjs-on-cloudflare: Build, migrate, and deploy Next.js apps on Cloudflare Workers with vinext. For setup, migration, or deployment, install vinext's upstream skills with `npx skills add cloudflare/vinext` if missing, then read and follow the applicable skill and docs. (file: r0/nextjs-on-cloudflare/SKILL.md)
- plugin-management:plugin-management: Discover and suggest relevant plugins, inspect app permissions and dependencies, and manage plugin connections or removal. Use when the user asks about plugins or when a task would materially benefit from an external app, account, service, or data source that available tools cannot access. (file: r2/plugin-management/0.1.0/skills/plugin-management/SKILL.md)

Load when building AI code execution, code interpreters, CI/CD systems, interactive dev environments, or executing untrusted code. (file: r3/sites/SKILL.md)

settings.developer_instructions:
# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

---
name: using-entire
description: >
  Use for any codebase exploration or understanding task — reads historical
  intent from Entire checkpoints instead of guessing. Orchestrates other Entire
  skills to give the agent provenance-backed answers about code.
---

# Using Entire

Your default when exploring or understanding code should be: **read the
recorded intent, don't guess.**

Entire checkpoints capture the prompts, transcripts, and decisions behind every
agent-driven change. When you need to understand why code exists or how a module
evolved, look up the checkpoint history first. Only fall back to inference from
code structure when no history is available — and label that explicitly.

## When This Skill Activates

Use this skill whenever the task involves:

- Exploring or understanding an unfamiliar module or file
- Preparing to refactor, extend, or debug code you didn't write
- Answering "why is this like this?" or "what was the intent?"
- Doing pre-work research before making changes
- Any codebase exploration where historical context would help

Do **not** use this skill for simple, well-understood edits where you already
have full context (e.g. "add a comment to line 5").

## First Step: Check Repository Status

Before diving into specific lookups, check whether Entire is available and
the repository has checkpoint history:

```bash
entire status
```

This tells you whether Entire is enabled, which git hooks are installed, whether
the metadata branch is initialized, and any active sessions on the current
branch.

## Scenario Routing

When this skill activates, determine which sub-skill best fits the user's need:

| Scenario | Typical user expressions | Delegate to |
|----------|------------------------|-------------|
| Code block provenance | "why is this like this" / "wtf is going on" / "what happened at src/auth.ts:42" / "tell me why this changed" | `what-happened` |
| Find prior work | "has anyone done X before" / "search past work for rate limiting" / "find the previous implementation" | `search` |
| Understand original intent | "explain this function" / "explain parseConfig" / "what was the intent behind src/auth.ts" | `explain` |
| Generate a dispatch / summary | "summarize recent work" / "generate a dispatch" / "what was accomplished this week" | run `entire dispatch` directly |
| Code review with intent context | "review these changes" / "review this branch" / "audit before merging" | `review` |
| Hand off to another agent | "hand off this session" / "continue in another agent" / "pick up the codex session" | `session-handoff` |
| Convert session to skill | "turn this into a skill" / "make a skill from this session" | `session-to-skill` |
| Link session to other repos | "link session to other repos" / "attach session to the foo repo" | `session-crosslink` |
| General exploration | "understand this module" / "explore how auth works" / "help me understand the codebase" | _(self — see below)_ |

If the scenario clearly maps to a sub-skill, delegate entirely to that skill's
workflow. Do not duplicate their steps here.

## General Exploration Flow

When no specific sub-skill fits — e.g. the user asks to "understand this
module" or "explore how auth works" — use this flow:

1. **Identify key files** in the target area (entry points, main types, core
   functions).

2. **Check for checkpoint coverage** on each key file:

```bash
git log --format='%H %s' -5 -- <file>
```

Look for `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers in the commit bodies:

```bash
git log --format='%H %b' -5 -- <file> | grep -B1 'Entire-Checkpoint:'
```

3. **Read intent for covered commits** — extract the checkpoint ID from the
   trailer, then use JSON output for non-interactive consumption:

```bash
entire explain --checkpoint <checkpoint-id> --json --no-pager
```

If you only have a commit hash (not a checkpoint ID), use:

```bash
entire explain --commit <sha> --no-pager
```

4. **Synthesize**: combine the recorded intent (from checkpoints) with the
   current code structure to build a comprehensive understanding.

5. **Report** your findings, clearly distinguishing:
   - Facts backed by checkpoint transcripts (label as "recorded intent")
   - Observations inferred from code alone (label as "inferred from code")

## AI Agent Usage Notes

When running Entire commands from an agent subprocess:

- **Always pass `--json`** for commands that support it and might prompt
  interactively. `--json` implies non-interactive output.
- **Always pass `--no-pager`** to prevent pager activation in subprocess
  contexts.
- **Always specify `--checkpoint <id>` or `--commit <sha>`** for
  `entire explain` — without a locator, the command falls back to an
  interactive picker.

## When No Checkpoints Exist

If the target code predates Entire or has no checkpoint coverage:

1. Say explicitly: "No Entire checkpoint history is available for this code."
2. Proceed with standard code understanding (read source, check git log, trace
   call sites).
3. Label all explanations as "inferred from code — not backed by recorded
   intent."
4. If the user wants deeper history, suggest `search` with related keywords —
   there may be checkpoints on related work even if the specific file isn't
   directly covered.

## Transparency Principle

Always make it clear whether your answer comes from:

- **Checkpoint-backed history** — you read the actual session transcript and
  know the developer's stated intent
- **Code inference** — you analyzed the code structure and are reasoning about
  probable intent

Never present inferred intent as if it were recorded fact. The core value of
this workflow is that distinction.

## References

For a deeper understanding of Entire's capabilities beyond what the sub-skills
cover, consult these resources:

- **CLI help**: run `entire help` to see all available commands and flags
- **Documentation**: https://docs.entire.io/llms.txt — AI-friendly
  documentation index following the [llms.txt standard](https://llmstxt.org),
  designed to be consumed directly by LLMs and coding agents
---
name: agent-tools
description: Use JSHack's deterministic inspection and architecture tools to locate behavior, verify boundaries, and gather evidence before changing code.
argument-hint: <question-or-target>
---

Use this skill when a task needs repository-wide discovery, architecture evidence,
event wiring analysis, scheduler mapping, content-ID tracing, or a health check.
These tools are read-only unless a command explicitly says otherwise. Their
canonical implementations live beside this guide in `scripts/`; invoke them
from the repository root and prefer the smallest output mode that answers the
question.

## Start with the question

Choose the route before searching broadly:

| Need | Tool | First command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Find a symbol, event, file, or test | `agent-target` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/agent-target.mjs TERM --limit 80` |
| Trace an item, monster, spell, material, loot, or visual ID | `content-id-audit` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/content-id-audit.mjs ID --limit 80` |
| Inventory item rarity slots and find legacy/mismatched labels | `item-rarity-audit` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/item-rarity-audit.mjs --gear-only --format csv` |
| Find proc-package gear missing authored Equip mechanics | `proc-gear-audit` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/proc-gear-audit.mjs --unconverted` |
| Compare same-slot gear and flag obvious strength outliers | `item-strength-audit` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/item-strength-audit.mjs --outliers --format csv` |
| Understand event producers and consumers | `event-bus-explorer` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format summary --top 40` |
| Validate a quest-backed dungeon | `quest-content-audit` | `deno task audit:quests` |
| Inspect one event contract | `event-bus-explorer` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format csv --event EVENT` |
| Map scheduler registration and phases | `system-map` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs --format summary` |
| Find unregistered or untested systems | `system-map` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/system-map.mjs --unregistered` or `--missing-tests` |
| Check architecture hazards | `agent-health` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/agent-health.mjs` |
| Inspect import-layer violations | `import-boundary-report` | `deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/import-boundary-report.mjs` |

## Evidence workflow

1. Run the narrowest relevant command before reading unrelated source.
2. Follow tool results to the named files, systems, tests, or event contracts.
3. Check scheduler registration and layer boundaries when the change crosses
   rules, bridge, display, or main.
4. Check event producers and consumers when adding or changing an event.
5. Use `content-id-audit` before changing content-facing definitions so every
   canonical reference and presentation path is known.
6. Run `deno test --allow-read tests/agentTools.test.mjs` if tool behavior or
   parsing assumptions change.

## Class identity/display verification

When adding or changing a player class, treat its identity as a cross-layer
contract. Verify all of these independently:

- `CLASS_DEFS` registration, valid deity, starter equipment, inventory, and spells.
- A fresh runtime applies `player_<classId>` to `NamedIdentity` and projects the
  same value through `WorldView`.
- `applyPlayerClassLoadout()` repairs the identity when the player entity
  already exists; this covers the live new-game path after entity creation.
- `buildPalette()` contains `player_<classId>` and the glyph atlas can resolve it.

The smallest useful regression set is:

```bash
deno test --allow-read tests/classes.test.mjs tests/agentRuntime.test.mjs tests/displayGlyphCoverage.test.mjs
```

Do not validate only the palette row: a correct palette cannot fix a stale or
generic `NamedIdentity` reaching the bridge.

## Useful output modes

- `summary` is for a fast human scan.
- `csv` is for exact producer/consumer or reference inspection.
- `mermaid` is for visualizing event relationships.
- `--producer-only` and `--consumer-only` expose orphaned event wiring.
- `--phase`, `--unregistered`, and `--missing-tests` focus the system map.

## Guardrails

- Treat reports as evidence, not as permission to delete apparently unused
  files. Listener installers and dynamic references can be intentionally absent
  from static registration results.
- Keep tool changes deterministic, import-safe, and usable with `--allow-read`.
- `quest-content-audit` checks quest tracker/template parity, authored landmark
  entrances, and explicit monster IDs using the existing content fields.
- Extend existing tools when a question recurs; do not add a one-off grep script
  for a query they can already answer.
- When a new recurring workflow is proven, update this skill with the route and
  validation command rather than creating duplicate guidance elsewhere.

Use this skill to discover canonical code and event/scheduler ownership, then
hand off seeded behavior proof to `runtime-tools`. Producer-only and
consumer-only reports require manual classification; imported-but-unregistered
systems may be listener installers. Do not delete from reports alone.

## Related project tasks

```bash
deno task guard:architecture
deno task guard:events
deno task guard:tools
deno task audit:health
deno task audit:events
deno task audit:systems
deno task audit:quests
```

issue.title: ARCH/UX: Canonicalize Character Statistics, Simplify Presentation, and Preserve Build Diversity
issue.body:
## Summary

JS Hack has accumulated a sophisticated statistical model supporting physical combat, ranged weapons, spellcasting, healing, resource management, equipment, enchantments, affixes, and unusual mechanical interactions.

Much of this complexity is intentional.

The problem is that the statistical model has become more complicated to **understand** than it needs to be. Player-facing interfaces expose overlapping concepts, internal calculations, inconsistent terminology, and information derived through different resolution paths.

This issue proposes a comprehensive audit, canonicalization, and presentation pass.

**The objective is not to reduce the mechanical depth of JS Hack. It is to make that depth understandable while preserving meaningful equipment, hybrid characters, and extraordinary builds.**

> **Minimize the number of statistics players must understand. Maximize the meaningful ways those statistics and mechanics can interact.**

JS Hack is not an MMORPG. It should not accumulate additional statistical categories merely to create more opportunities for numerical optimization. Conversely, statistical simplification must not flatten equipment, eliminate meaningful tradeoffs, or constrain character development.

**Related:** #172 — Research Stat Scaling and Item Power Budgets. This issue concerns semantic coherence, effective-stat correctness, and presentation; #172 handles numerical curves and item power budgets.

## Design Philosophy

### Simple statistics. Complicated consequences.

Numerical bonuses make builds stronger. Mechanical interactions make builds different.

A weapon that restores Mana on critical strikes can enable a spell that interacts with another equipped artifact, producing a new playstyle without creating a new permanent character statistic. The statistical system supplies the foundation; passive expressions and procs supply the possibilities.

**Do not sacrifice emergent behavior to simplify the interface.**

### Preserve the universal character model

Every player class has Health, Mana, and Stamina, can engage in physical combat, can use ranged equipment, and participates in shared equipment and statistical systems.

Classes primarily establish identity, starting attributes, equipment, spells, and thematic relationships. They must not dictate separate statistical models. A Cleric may become a melee combatant; a Warden may acquire magic; a Mage may discover physical-combat synergies.

> **Class determines where a character begins. Equipment, abilities, and decisions determine what that character becomes.**

Do not introduce class-specific statistical restrictions. Preserve the option for eventual formal multiclassing without requiring it for hybrid playstyles.

---

## 1. Inventory and Classify Existing Statistics

Audit the existing system before designing a replacement taxonomy. Proposed *organizational* categories—not required new ECS abstractions:

| Category | Current examples | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Primary attributes | Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Vitality | Broad characteristics |
| Resources | Health, Mana, Stamina | Current consumable/recoverable state |
| Resource statistics | Maximum HP/Mana/Stamina, regeneration | Capacity and sustainability |
| Secondary statistics | Accuracy, Damage Power, Critical Strike, Spell Power | Broad capabilities |
| Defensive statistics | Evade, Mitigation, AC, Kinetic DR | Hit prevention and damage mitigation |
| Action outcomes | Weapon damage, spell damage, healing | Results of actions |
| Contextual statistics | Resistances, penetration, vision, speed, encumbrance | Specialized behavior |
| Exceptional mechanics | Procs, curses, blessings, Hamingja, deity effects | Unusual and conditional behavior |

**Stamina is a statistic and a resource.** Maximum Stamina and Stamina Regeneration are statistics as well, as are the analogous Mana and Health values.

**Primary attribute set remains unsettled.** The current four (Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Vitality) are the baseline. Do not add Spirit, Perception, or Luck merely to reach a desired count. SPECIAL-inspired star visualization is a possible UI treatment, not a mandate to adopt seven attributes.

**Required audit for every channel:** identifier, definition, units, valid range, authored sources, gear/effect contributors, stacking and rounding, caps, actual consumers, presentation consumers, and genuine independence versus semantic duplication. Trace behavior through code rather than inferring it from labels.

**Deliverable:** Current-state inventory, producer-to-consumer map, and candidate canonical vocabulary.

## 2. Preserve Direct Equipment Contributions at Every Appropriate Layer

Gear must be able to contribute **directly** to:
- Primary attributes.
- Secondary statistics.
- Resource maximums and regeneration.
- Action-specific capabilities.
- Triggered/conditional behavior.

Do not route a Mana bonus through Intelligence, or an Accuracy bonus through Dexterity, merely to fit a narrow primary-stat model.

Existing examples:

```js
// Oak Staff
bonuses: {
  accuracy: 1,
  damagePower: 1,
  bluntPenetration: 1,
  manaRegen: 0.05
}

// Mossguard Mail
bonuses: {
  defense: 2,
  maxHp: 4,
  poisonResist: 0.05
}
```

Preserve this existing expressiveness. The problem is inconsistent authoring semantics: `ItemInfo.bonuses`, affix passive scripts, `DerivedExpression`, and canonical resolution accept overlapping but nonidentical keys. `spellPower`, for instance, is expression-supported but not recognized by the ordinary item bonus mapping.

Legacy `attack` equipment bonuses currently modify both Accuracy and Damage Power; `defense` maps to Evade. These aliases are ambiguous and require a documented migration/compatibility plan.

**Requirements:**
- One canonical identifier and meaning per supported contribution.
- Direct secondary/resource bonuses remain supported.
- Migration or compatibility for all existing authored content.
- Preserve gems, sockets, enchantments, affixes, attached expressions, and topology.
- Avoid silently converting one stat into unrelated bonuses.
- Avoid double-applying bonuses through compatibility pathways.
- Explain the contribution of a specific item to effective results.

## 3. Defensive Vocabulary: Avoidance and Armor; Retire Player-Facing DR

Current defensive presentation fragments Defense, Evade, Armor Class, Mitigation, Kinetic DR, typed resistances, and conditional effects. The HUD also synthesizes `DEF%` by adding physical damage reduction to an AC contribution—quantities with incompatible meanings.

Proposed player-facing **concepts**:

**Avoidance — Will the attack connect?** Hit prevention through evasion, dodging, parrying, posture, and appropriate effects. Internal AC and individual avoidance rolls may remain. Do not claim this is a universal hit probability without a defined attack context.

**Armor — How much will it hurt if it connects?** Physical damage reduction from worn equipment, natural resilience, magical reinforcement, or temporary effects. Armor need not originate from an armor item.

**Do not simply rename `kineticDR` to `armor`.** The simulation combines flat DR, mitigation, typed multipliers, and penetration; a displayed Armor value needs a specified, defensible projection. If no universal scalar accurately captures all physical damage, qualify a representative value and retain detailed typed information.

Tasks:
- Remove **Kinetic DR** from ordinary player-facing labels; preserve its underlying mechanics.
- Remove/replace the misleading `DEF%` composite.
- Resolve duplicated Defense/Evade presentation.
- Consider AC a detail/debug implementation concept.
- Document the units and meaning of displayed Avoidance and Armor.
- Preserve typed resistance, immunity, penetration, and special defense behavior.
- Do not silently rebalance hit rolls or damage mitigation.

## 4. Preserve Dice Distributions; Display Average Weapon Damage

**Do not replace dice-based damage with fixed damage.**

The distribution is part of weapon identity. An axe may produce volatile highs and lows; a multi-die weapon may be more consistent. The ordinary interface should display a **single representative expected damage number** while preserving these qualitative differences in the simulation.

Illustrative profiles (not a reassignment of authored weapon definitions):

| Internal dice | Mathematical mean | Displayed Damage |
|---|---:|---:|
| `1d4` | 2.5 | **3** |
| `1d6` | 3.5 | **4** |
| `1d8` | 4.5 | **5** |
| `1d12` | 6.5 | **7** |
| `2d6` | 7.0 | **7** |

`1d12` and `2d6` may display the same Damage while retaining very different distributions.

**Calculation contract:**
- Distinguish intrinsic item damage distribution from the *effective* expected damage with this character's equipment, primary/secondary bonuses, and always-applicable modifiers.
- Show expectation **conditional on an ordinary successful hit**, before target-specific mitigation and critical effects.
- Do **not** silently include arbitrary opponent hit probability, target-specific resistance, proc damage, or rare conditional outcomes.
- Specify one rounding policy (illustratively, `Math.round` for positive expected damage).
- Respect the actual execution order, flooring, clamping, and nonlinear modifiers: evaluating a transform at the mean does not necessarily equal the mean of transformed rolls.
- The HUD currently uses `averageDice()` in `src/main/ui/hudFeeds.js`; treat this as precedent, not proof that its estimated full-pipeline damage is exact.
- Establish a shared deterministic projection for HUD, tooltip, character detail, and equipment comparison. No duplicated UI-specific formulas.
- Equipment comparisons must evaluate outcomes for the same character before/after hypothetical item replacement **without mutating the live world**.
- Preserve optional detailed ranges/distributions, and communicate meaningful costs, attributes, and proc tradeoffs without inventing a global Variance stat.

**Acceptance:** `1d12` and `2d6` display equal rounded averages but remain different in real damage rolls; every UI reports the same context-appropriate expected value. No changes to stochastic mechanics or seeded RNG.

> **Preserve the distribution. Present the expectation.**

## 5. Treat Health, Mana, and Stamina as First-Class Statistics

The existing resource model is real gameplay, not an adjacent non-stat layer.

- **Health:** current HP, effective maximum HP, healing/recovery.
- **Mana:** current Mana, effective maximum, regeneration, regen cooldown, hunger/context effects.
- **Stamina:** current Stamina, effective maximum, regeneration, regen cooldown, encumbrance/context effects.

Existing gear bonuses to `maxHp`, `maxMana`, `maxStamina`, `manaRegen`, and `staminaRegen` are important and must continue to work.

`manaRegenerationSystem.js` calculates base + passive + expression-derived modifiers, modified by hunger. `staminaRegenerationSystem.js` calculates base + passive + expression-derived modifiers, modified by encumbrance. Both enforce post-expenditure cooldowns.

The current character sheet does not show all inputs used by the regen systems. It also reads `Vitality.maxHp` without the equipment-derived bonus already included by the HUD's effective-max logic.

Tasks:
- Canonicalize effective resource maximums and recovery projections.
- Ensure HUD, character sheet, and detailed views use consistent authority.
- Distinguish underlying regeneration capability from temporarily suppressed/modified effective recovery.
- Preserve resource-specific expenditure, recovery, and cooldown semantics.
- Do not collapse resource state into a monolithic stat component.

Illustrative presentation:

```text
Health       22 / 22
Mana         65 / 69     +0.44/turn
Stamina      77 / 83     +2.2/turn
```

## 6. Establish Consistent Accuracy and Critical Strike Semantics

**Accuracy is not Damage.** The character sheet's Attack is a to-hit modifier, while HUD Atk is estimated weapon damage. Eliminate this label collision.

Separate: Accuracy, hit roll, opponent-dependent hit chance, and expected successful-hit damage.

Critical channels currently include:

```text
critChancePhysical
critChanceSpell
critMultPhysical
critMultSpell
```

Different physical, spell, and (where intentionally supported) healing critical rules may remain. They do not necessarily require an equally fragmented **equipment itemization vocabulary**.

Audit whether shared gear critical bonuses apply to all intended eligible actions; whether narrowly scoped bonuses stay scoped; and why some spell damage obtains critical values through a physical combat snapshot despite the separate spell-critical channel.

Document eligibility, units (fraction vs percent), caps, multipliers, conditional boosts, and source precedence. Do not assume every healing spell can crit or force identical formulas on every action.

**Acceptance:** General and action-specific critical contributions have explicit semantics and reach their intended consumers; legacy content retains intended behavior.

## 7. Preserve Offensive Magic, Healing, and Hybrid Capabilities

Do not make the stat design melee-centric or class-specific.

Review the interplay of:
- `BaseStats.intelligence`.
- `Brain.intelligence`.
- Resolved `spellPower`.
- Canonical spell hit/avoid calculations.
- Individual spell damage and healing scripts.
- `HealingModifiers` and `applyHealing()`.

Current healing formulas are not uniform; some scale from `Brain.intelligence` directly. Audit and reconcile supported statistical contributions, but **do not force every spell to use one formula**.

Player-facing spell details should communicate understandable effective outcomes where reliable (damage, healing, cost, range, duration) rather than requiring players to inspect an expression graph.

An item intended to improve healing must have an explicit, predictable route to the relevant ability; do not automatically invent global Healing Power if existing channels and scoped modifiers suffice.

A character's starting class must not dictate which abilities can consume the character's statistical contributions.

## 8. Preserve the Passive / Proc Architecture

Read `docs/architecture/FINAL_STATS_PROC_ARCHITECTURE.md` first.

Maintain the strict split:

**Passive:** What is true about the actor now? `BaseStats`, `DerivedExpression`, `ResolvedStats`, `PassiveBonuses`, equipped hierarchy, and authored continuous contributions.

**Proc:** What occurs when a particular event passes through attached topology? `ProcNode`, `ActivationGate`, `ProcEffect`, `ScriptRef`, accumulator, separate application phase.

Example hybrid artifact:

```text
Maximum Mana       +10
Critical Strike     +3%

On Critical Hit:
  Restore 3 Mana
```

The first effects are passive. The restore is event-triggered. No new global stat is necessary.

Preserve hierarchy-aware evaluation, deterministic ordering/RNG, proc accumulator/application separation, and script escape hatches. Do not reintroduce combat callback soup or direct arbitrary mutation from proc evaluation.

Preserve the distinction between Hamingja's contribution to Luck and its lineage-associated narrative/source metadata. Do not flatten special world mechanics into generic ratings.

## 9. Canonicalize Resolution Without Replacing ECS

Important starting points:

```text
src/rules/components/BaseStats.js
src/rules/components/Mana.js
src/rules/components/Stamina.js
src/rules/components/Vitality.js
src/rules/components/Equipment.js
src/rules/components/DerivedExpression.js
src/rules/utils/derivedStats.js
src/rules/utils/passiveBonuses.js
src/rules/utils/canonicalStats.js
src/rules/utils/resolveCombatSnapshot.js
src/rules/utils/statProcAuthoring.js
src/rules/utils/spellDamage.js
src/rules/utils/applyHealing.js
src/rules/utils/dealDamage.js
src/rules/systems/manaRegenerationSystem.js
src/rules/systems/staminaRegenerationSystem.js
src/rules/systems/combatSystem.js
src/rules/systems/rangedAttackSystem.js
src/rules/systems/castSpellSystem.js
src/main/ui/hudFeeds.js
src/main/ui/inventoryDataProvider.js
src/display/ui/characterOverlay.js
src/display/ui/overlayUtils.js
docs/architecture/FINAL_STATS_PROC_ARCHITECTURE.md
docs/architecture/STAT_PIPELINE_TECHNICAL_MEMO.md
docs/architecture/DAMAGE_PIPELINE_TECHNICAL_MEMO.md
```

The documented hybrid resolution consists of `BaseStats` / expressions / `ResolvedStats` and equipment / affix / `PassiveBonuses` merging through canonical combat projection. Resource components and regeneration systems own additional effective values. Compatibility is intentional; inconsistent consumer interpretations are not.

**Desired:** One coherent effective-stat **read contract**, without one giant ECS record or a second competing engine.

Every channel needs explicit meaning, unit, combining stage/order, sources, consumer scope, caps, and rounding. Existing facilities such as `explainDerivedStats()` should be extended where practical to explain complete provenance.

Beware duplicated contributions when mixing `getResolvedStats()`, `getPassiveBonuses()`, and `resolveCanonicalStats()`: they are not interchangeable. Regression-test before replacing consumers.

## 10. Rework Character Sheet, HUD, and Item Presentation

Organize ordinary presentation around:

**Attributes** — Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Vitality (final primary taxonomy open).

**Resources** — Health, Mana, Stamina with effective maximums and meaningful recovery information.

**Capabilities** — concise and truly distinct values such as Accuracy, Avoidance, Armor, Critical Strike, relevant spell capability.

**Additional Details** — typed resistances, penetration, movement, encumbrance, crit multipliers, traits, and unusual effects remain inspectable, not necessarily permanently displayed.

Illustrative sheet (numbers do not prescribe formulas):

```text
ATTRIBUTES
Strength          10
Dexterity         12
Intelligence      13
Vitality          10

RESOURCES
Health           22 / 22
Mana             65 / 69      +0.44/turn
Stamina          77 / 83      +2.2/turn

CAPABILITIES
Accuracy         +3
Avoidance        +2
Armor             4
Critical Strike   4%
Spell Power      13
```

This is *conceptual organization*, not a mandatory wireframe.

- One vocabulary across all starting classes.
- The HUD displays immediate gameplay information, not redundant implementation detail.
- Item tooltips distinguish intrinsic properties, direct bonuses, effective action outcomes, and exceptional mechanics.
- Comparisons show meaningful deltas and costs, not merely a synthetic power score.
- Do not expose raw proc-node or ECS structure in ordinary item tooltips.
- Preserve advanced detail/debug inspection.
- Validate desktop and mobile layouts.

## 11. Known Code-Level Reconciliation Targets

| Area | Observation | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| Character-sheet Attack | To-hit modifier | Disambiguate from damage |
| HUD Atk | Estimated weapon damage | Canonical expected-damage projection |
| Defense / Evade | Overlapping sheet values | Clarify Avoidance |
| HUD `DEF%` | Physical reduction plus AC contribution | Eliminate invalid composite |
| Kinetic DR | Player-visible internal stat | Retire terminology; preserve mechanics |
| Maximum Health | Sheet omits equipment bonus accounted for in HUD | Shared effective max |
| Mana Regeneration | Display omits some runtime modifiers | Authoritative effective rate |
| Stamina Regeneration | Display omits some runtime modifiers | Authoritative effective rate |
| Critical Strike | Physical/spell consumer inconsistency | Audit and define semantics |
| Healing | Several direct spell scaling paths | Audit supported contributions |
| Equipment `attack` | Changes Accuracy and Damage Power | Deprecate ambiguous alias |
| Equipment `defense` | Maps to Evade | Normalize meaning |
| `spellPower` | Expression target but not ordinary gear bonus key | Reconcile vocabulary |

Classify each as presentation defect, compatibility/semantic defect, or mechanical defect **before** changing it. No silent rebalancing.

## 12. Implementation Sequence

### Phase A — Inventory and baseline
- [ ] Read architecture docs and current code, not just this proposal.
- [ ] Enumerate all channels, units, authored sources, gear keys, affixes, and consumers.
- [ ] Record current physical, ranged, spell, healing, resource, critical, and defense behavior.
- [ ] Identify ambiguous/duplicate meanings.
- [ ] Establish deterministic baseline tests.
- [ ] Produce current-state inventory and proposed canonical vocabulary.

### Phase B — Statistical contract
- [ ] Define canonical identifiers, units, scopes, ordering, caps, and rounding.
- [ ] Define resource-stat semantics.
- [ ] Keep direct secondary and resource equipment contributions first-class.
- [ ] Define defensible Avoidance and Armor projections.
- [ ] Define shared vs scoped critical contributions.
- [ ] Plan migration/compatibility for `attack` and `defense`.
- [ ] Preserve all existing authored content.

### Phase C — Effective read models
- [ ] Reconcile Health, Mana, Stamina maximums and regeneration views.
- [ ] Consolidate redundant stat interpretation where practical.
- [ ] Provide shared, context-aware character projections.
- [ ] Provide authoritative damage expectation.
- [ ] Support read-only hypothetical equipment comparisons.
- [ ] Extend provenance for debugging and explainability.
- [ ] Verify modifiers are not double-applied.

### Phase D — Damage presentation
- [ ] Preserve dice distributions and seeded rolls.
- [ ] Define expected-damage and rounding contract.
- [ ] Replace ordinary dice text with single numerical weapon Damage.
- [ ] Update melee and ranged tooltips, HUD, equipment comparisons.
- [ ] Preserve optional detailed distribution/range inspection.
- [ ] Test parity of the underlying damage pipeline.

### Phase E — Sheet / HUD UX
- [ ] Reorganize attributes/resources/capabilities.
- [ ] Retire player-facing DR and unnecessary internal terminology.
- [ ] Resolve Avoidance vs Armor displays.
- [ ] Remove misleading `DEF%`.
- [ ] Disambiguate Attack/Accuracy/Damage.
- [ ] Align effective resource maximum/recovery displays.
- [ ] Keep specialized details accessible.
- [ ] Test desktop/mobile and all starting classes.

### Phase F — Verification and documentation
- [ ] Verify melee, ranged, spell, healing, resource, critical, and typed-defense parity.
- [ ] Verify plain gear, mixed bonuses, affixes, enchantments, gems, and procs.
- [ ] Verify equip/unequip, replacement, and compare previews.
- [ ] Verify save/load and deterministic replay behavior.
- [ ] Verify hybrid builds without class-based assumptions.
- [ ] Run the full relevant test suite and fix failures introduced by the work.
- [ ] Document mechanical questions requiring independent balance decisions.
- [ ] Update architectural handoff and stat vocabulary documentation.

## 13. Testing Requirements

Tests must cover behavior—not just rendered snapshots.

**Resources:** Each effective maximum and regeneration bonus separately and in combination; hunger, load, and cooldown effects; HUD/sheet parity.

**Equipment:** Plain gear; primary bonuses; direct secondary bonuses; resource bonuses; mixed bonuses; affixes; gems; enchantments; attached expressions; procs; equip/unequip/replacement; no double application.

**Damage:** At minimum, verify these exact mean/rounding examples:

```text
1d4   → 2.5 → displayed 3
1d6   → 3.5 → displayed 4
1d8   → 4.5 → displayed 5
1d12  → 6.5 → displayed 7
2d6   → 7.0 → displayed 7
```

Also test equal displayed averages with different underlying distributions, character-specific bonuses, rounding/flooring edge cases, no target-specific damage leakage, no gameplay RNG changes, and HUD/tooltip/comparison agreement.

**Defense:** Existing hit avoidance, damage reduction, typed resistance, penetration, and immunities unchanged; presented Armor/Avoidance correctly defined; `DEF%` composite gone.

**Hybrids:** Physical, ranged, offensive spell, healing, resource-intensive, and weird passive/proc combinations on characters regardless of starting class.

**Regression:** Presentation and nomenclature changes must not change gameplay results. Mechanically justified corrections require isolated tests and explicit documentation.

## 14. Explicit Non-Goals

This issue does **not** authorize:
- Fixed damage replacing dice distributions.
- Removal of legitimate resource stats or equipment contributions.
- New primary attributes, a mandatory seven-attribute SPECIAL model, or WoW-style Mastery.
- Class locks or implementation of a formal multiclass progression system.
- Replacement of ECS, passive expressions, or proc topology.
- A second competing stat resolver.
- Removal of typed damage/resistances.
- Flattening unusual affix/gear behavior.
- A wholesale combat rebalance.
- Transplanting diminishing-return curves or item-budget formulas from WoW.

Numerical curve and item-budget research remains **#172**.

## 15. Definition of Done

- [ ] Every displayed statistic has a documented, consistent meaning.
- [ ] Primary, secondary, resource, and contextual stats are coherently inventoried.
- [ ] Direct secondary/resource equipment contributions survive and resolve consistently.
- [ ] Existing equipment/affix/enchantment content remains functional.
- [ ] Sheet, HUD, and comparisons agree on effective resources and recovery.
- [ ] Accuracy, to-hit, and damage are not conflated.
- [ ] Avoidance and Armor are distinct, defensible concepts.
- [ ] DR is not ordinary player-facing terminology; underlying mechanics remain.
- [ ] The invalid composite `DEF%` has been removed.
- [ ] Critical bonuses have explicit scope and consistent consumers.
- [ ] Ordinary weapon damage is shown as one rounded expected value.
- [ ] Original stochastic damage distributions and deterministic RNG are intact.
- [ ] Item comparisons show context-aware effects and meaningful tradeoffs.
- [ ] The character sheet is substantially clearer without concealing build possibilities.
- [ ] Hybrid physical/ranged/magical/healing playstyles remain possible.
- [ ] Passive/proc separation remains intact.
- [ ] Behavioral changes, if any, are independently justified, tested, and documented.
- [ ] Relevant tests pass and documentation matches implementation.

---

## Final Design Direction

JS Hack should not require players to understand internal calculations to make meaningful decisions.

A dagger and an axe may show comparable damage averages while retaining different underlying distributions. A robe can improve Mana Regeneration without increasing Intelligence. A Cleric can fight in melee; a Warden can use magic. An unusual artifact can interact with another effect in ways nobody planned.

The character sheet describes the character. Equipment descriptions communicate contributions and tradeoffs. Abilities describe expected outcomes. The simulation retains all the mechanics.

> **Preserve the distribution. Present the expectation.**
>
> **Preserve the mechanics. Simplify the vocabulary.**
>
> **Preserve the classes. Remove artificial boundaries.**
>
> **Preserve the equipment. Let the builds get insane.**
>
> **JS Hack should be easy to understand and difficult to exhaust.**
